title: A Randomized Trial of Drug Route in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
shortTitle: PARAMEDIC-3: IO-first access did not improve survival
summary: PARAMEDIC-3 randomized 6,082 adults with OHCA requiring drug access to an IO-first or IV-first strategy. Thirty-day survival was 4.5% versus 5.1% (adjusted OR 0.94; 95% CI 0.68–1.32; P=.74). Favorable neurologic outcome at discharge was 2.7% versus 2.8%.
whyItMatters: Rapid IO placement alone is not evidence of a survival advantage over starting with IV access. Preserve IO as an alternative when IV access is unsuccessful or impractical.
limitations: Open-label pragmatic strategy trial in 11 UK EMS systems. Low survival and wide confidence intervals limit certainty about modest differences; secondary analyses were not adjusted for multiplicity.
population: Adults with OHCA needing vascular access for drug treatment.
findings: Any ROSC: 36.0% versus 39.1%; adjusted OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.76–0.97).
One adverse event was reported in the IO group.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. PubMed primary abstract and electronic publication date reviewed; the legal PMC author manuscript is available but was not reviewed in full.
